h1: The 6 Best Loppers Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 loppers under $100 compared on cut capacity, bypass versus anvil blades, leverage mechanism, handle length and steel quality.
summary: The Fiskars 32 Inch PowerGear2 is the best lopper for most homeowners, with gear leverage and a 2 inch capacity for green branches. The Corona X Series Pro cuts up to 2.25 inches, the TABOR TOOLS anvil lopper is for dead wood, the WORKPRO adds gear force to a short handle, and the FELCO is the light, repairable choice.
intro: A lopper's stated capacity is the thickest branch it will cut on a good day, and the best way to buy one is to ignore the top number. Cutting at the limit bends blades and crushes live wood. Choose a lopper rated about half an inch above the branches you actually cut, then decide whether the blade is bypass or anvil, because that choice affects whether live wood heals cleanly or dies back.

We ranked six loppers from the listings: capacity, blade type, leverage mechanism, handle length, steel and build. Bypass blades slide past each other like scissors, which suits live, green growth. Anvil blades close onto a flat surface, which suits dead, dry wood but can crush live stems. Gear and compound mechanisms multiply force so the handles need not be longer.

products.name: Fiskars 32 Inch PowerGear2 Bypass Lopper
products.verdict: A 32 inch bypass lopper with PowerGear2 leverage, a 2 inch capacity and hardened steel.
products.description:
The Fiskars PowerGear2 is a 32 inch bypass lopper with PowerGear2 leverage, a 2 inch stated capacity and hardened bypass steel.

It ranks first because it combines the 2 inch capacity most homeowners need with gear leverage, so you cut thick green branches without a longer handle. It beats the 28 inch Fiskars on capacity, 2 inches against 1.5, and the WORKPRO on reach. The Corona cuts 2.25 inches, a bit more, and costs more.

Buy it if you cut thick green branches and overhead growth. Skip it if you want the lightest tool. The weight is the price you pay for the extra reach and force, so test it overhead before committing.
cons: Gear adds a part that can wear
products.idealFor: Homeowners cutting thick green branches and overhead growth.

products.name: Corona Clipper X Series Pro Bypass Lopper
products.verdict: A pro-grade bypass lopper with a 2.25 inch capacity for trees and shrubs.
products.description:
The Corona X Series Pro is a bypass lopper with a 2.25 inch stated capacity, pro-grade build and a heavy-duty cutter for trees and shrubs.

It ranks second because it cuts the thickest branches here, a quarter inch above the Fiskars. It costs $50-100 and the listing gives no length or mechanism detail, so you cannot compare leverage directly with the PowerGear2.

Buy it if you cut live branches near 2 inches. Skip it if you want a documented gear mechanism. Its price is the premium for the thickest cut in this group, which suits owners with mature trees and shrubs.
products.idealFor: Heavy yard work with live branches near 2 inches.
products.skipIf: You want a stated gear mechanism.

products.name: TABOR TOOLS GG12A 30 Inch Anvil Lopper
products.verdict: A 30 inch anvil lopper with compound action and a 2 inch capacity.
products.description:
The TABOR TOOLS GG12A is a 30 inch anvil lopper with compound action and a 2 inch capacity.

It ranks third because an anvil blade clears dead, dry branches with less hand effort, and the compound action multiplies force. It loses to the bypass loppers for live growth, because an anvil crushes green stems and can leave a ragged cut.

Buy it if you clear dead wood. Skip it if you prune live shrubs. It also pairs well with a pruning saw for anything thicker than two inches, which no hand lopper here handles.

products.name: WORKPRO 28 Inch Gear Bypass Lopper, 1.5 Inch
products.verdict: A 28 inch gear bypass lopper with an SK5 steel blade, rated 1.5 inch.
products.description:
The WORKPRO is a 28 inch bypass lopper with a gear mechanism, an SK5 steel blade and a 1.5 inch capacity, under $25.

It ranks fourth because gear force on a short handle is a smart choice for small hands, but 1.5 inches caps the branch size. It beats the plain Fiskars 28 inch on force, since that model lacks a gear.

Buy it if you want extra cutting force without a long handle. Skip it if you cut 2 inch branches. A gear lopper is also easier for smaller gardeners, since force replaces long leverage.
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants extra force without a longer handle.

products.name: Fiskars 28 Inch Bypass Lopper, 1.5 Inch Cut
products.verdict: A 28 inch bypass lopper with a low-friction coating and 1.5 inch capacity.
products.description:
The Fiskars 28 inch Bypass is a simple bypass lopper with a low-friction coating and a 1.5 inch stated capacity.

It ranks fifth because it has no gear to multiply force, so it suits shrubs and shoots under an inch. It is under $25 and light.

Buy it if you trim shrubs. Skip it if you cut thick branches. It is the obvious entry-level tool for a first garden.
products.idealFor: Gardeners who trim shrubs and shoots under an inch.

products.name: FELCO F211-60 24 Inch Swiss Made Lopper
products.verdict: A 24 inch Swiss-made lopper with aluminum handles, carbon steel blades and micrometric adjustment.
products.description:
The FELCO F211-60 is a 24 inch lopper with lightweight aluminum handles, carbon steel blades and a micrometric adjustment.

It ranks last for raw power because it is short, but it is light and repairable, with a precise blade setting. It suits careful gardeners.

Buy it if you want a light tool you can maintain. Skip it if you need reach or force. Keep the adjustment bolt snug and the blades clean to get the most out of it.
products.idealFor: Careful gardeners who want a light tool.

whatMatters.detail: Capacity is the thickest branch a lopper cuts, from 1.5 to 2.25 inches here. Cutting at the limit stresses the blades. Check the stated figure, and choose half an inch above your real branch size. A tool rated for two inches will happily cut one, and the extra margin is what keeps the pivot tight for years.

Bypass blades pass each other like scissors and leave a clean cut on live wood. Anvil blades close onto a flat plate and suit dead wood. Check the blade type on the listing. Clean cuts matter for the plant, since a crushed stem heals slowly and invites disease.

Gear and compound action multiply your force so the handles can be shorter. The Fiskars uses PowerGear2 and the WORKPRO a gear system. Check the mechanism, and note it adds a part that can wear. Gears are the part to inspect if a lopper starts to feel gritty, because dirt and sap collect there first.

Longer handles give more reach and leverage but add weight. Lengths here run 24 to 32 inches. Check the length on the listing, and think about overhead cuts. If you cut overhead often, a long handle is a lever and a burden at once, so choose with your shoulders in mind.

SK5 and carbon steel hold an edge, and a repairable tool like the FELCO lets you replace parts. Check the blade steel and any note on replacement parts. Sap and rust are what ruin blades, so a tool you can clean and sharpen will outlive one you cannot.

faq.q: Can a lopper cut a branch as thick as its capacity?
faq.a: Only on dry, clean cuts. The Fiskars PowerGear2 lists 2 inches, but cutting live wood at the limit crushes it. Work a half inch below the figure. A sharp blade also reduces the force you need.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Using an anvil lopper on live shrubs. The TABOR TOOLS anvil crushes green stems, while a bypass like the Fiskars or Corona cuts cleanly. Match the blade type to the wood you cut.

faq.q: Is the PowerGear2 worth it over the WORKPRO?
faq.a: For thick branches, yes. The Fiskars PowerGear2 cuts 2 inches against the WORKPRO's 1.5, but the WORKPRO adds gear force under $25. Gear force helps most on dry wood.

faq.q: How do I set up a lopper?
faq.a: Check the pivot bolt is snug, and set the blade gap on adjustable models like the FELCO. A loose pivot tears wood. Oil the pivot once a season.

faq.q: How do I look after one?
faq.a: Wipe the blades after use, oil the pivot and sharpen the bypass edge on its bevel. Keep the FELCO's parts clean. Use a pruning saw for anything thicker.

faq.q: Can I cut wire or roots?
faq.a: No. Loppers are for wood, and wire or rocks nick the blades. Use a different tool for those. A tool that is too big for the job wastes effort.

finalTake: The Fiskars 32 Inch PowerGear2 Bypass Lopper is the best buy, with a 2 inch capacity and gear leverage. The Corona X Series Pro cuts a bit thicker, the TABOR TOOLS clears dead wood, and the FELCO is the light, repairable choice. Pick a lopper with half an inch of spare capacity.
